### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [X] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version

### Module(s)

mini.completion

### Description

Hey, Thanks for your awesome plugins!
tailwind has css class names like `m-{number}` so typing m- should bring completion menu like m-1, m-2, etc instead completion is showing wrong candidates:
![image](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/assets/27911493/295f4dd2-b40e-498a-9aeb-82d722372dd8)
while omnifunc returns
![image](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/assets/27911493/83fa716a-6beb-4714-a420-798debda1f7f)
     

### Neovim version

NVIM v0.9.4

### Steps to reproduce

1. create a svelte project: `npm init svelte`
2. press enter on every prompt
3. npm install
4. initialize tailwindcss according to https://tailwindcss.com/docs/guides/sveltekit
5. `nvim --clean -u minimal.lua src/routes/+layout.svelte`
6. cursor on line 6 column 16 and type `m-`

minimal.lua:
```
for name, url in pairs({
	"https://github.com/neovim/nvim-lspconfig/",
	"https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.completion",
}) do
	local install_path = vim.fn.fnamemodify("lspconfig/" .. name, ":p")
	if vim.fn.isdirectory(install_path) == 0 then
		vim.fn.system({ "git", "clone", "--depth=1", url, install_path })
		print("Installing " .. install_path)
	end
	vim.opt.runtimepath:append(install_path)
end

require("mini.completion").setup()

local lspconfig = require("lspconfig")
lspconfig.svelte.setup({})
lspconfig.tailwindcss.setup({})
```

### Expected behavior

to return same completion candidates as omnifunc

### Actual behavior

explained in description

Thanks for the issue!

Does the list of candidates look like that if completion is initiated with empty space to the left of cursor? It seems like `ml-` is not recognized as "base" for completion.

What does executing `:echo &iskeyword` show? For this to work, it should contain `-` as a symbol (it does not by default).

> Does the list of candidates look like that if completion is initiated with empty space to the left of cursor? It seems like ml- is not recognized as "base" for completion.

I'm not sure I understand what you mean by that, I'm not getting same completion with a space after `m-`

> What does executing :echo &iskeyword show? For this to work, it should contain - as a symbol (it does not by default).

Yes that makes it work though it's a not good idea to change that option globally as it will affect the vim word matching

> Yes that makes it work though it's a not good idea to change that option globally as it will affect the vim word matching

That is the whole point of this part of 'mini.completion' design: user wants to complete what is recognizable as "word". [Judging by the code](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/cff8f2bddbbc1093a9ffbf1122df918be5ff41d9/lua/mini/completion.lua#L1306), it was also the approach of built-in omnifunc. I'll take a look why these are different and revisit this.

I am not sure why built-in `vim.lsp.omnifunc` (I assume you used it in second example) give different complete word than 'mini.completion'. Here is the [code 'mini.completion' uses](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/cff8f2bddbbc1093a9ffbf1122df918be5ff41d9/lua/mini/completion.lua#L1306-L1310) and here is the [code of `vim.lsp.omnifunc`](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/a8fc94a2fdd07edf0679d34f2deaacb25b3fa69f/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L2323-L2330) (one vs zero indexing is dealt with in 'mini.completion' in other place).

~~The suggested approach here is to indeed include `-` in 'iskeyword' option (for example, with `vim.opt.iskeyword:append('-')`), as 'mini.completion' uses keyword to the left of cursor as the base for completion.~~ **Edit**: This should now (on at least latest `main`) work without tweaking 'iskeyword'. See [this comment](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/issues/530#issuecomment-2806924783) for more details.

@echasnovski this seems to be related https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/15784
`.` is not part of `iskeyword` why that trigger completion menu properly

Yes, indeed this might be the reason. Seems to complicate things rather severely when there is another good (not perfect, but good enough) solution.

> `.` is not part of `iskeyword` why that trigger completion menu properly

I'd suggest because language server provides proper candidates which respect that dot through cursor position (which also is sent to server).

@echasnovski sorry for sending noise to this closed issue, but using `omnifunc` as completion source fixes this issue
is there's any tradeoff in using `omnifunc`? and why it's not used by default?

> @echasnovski sorry for sending noise to this closed issue, but using `omnifunc` as completion source fixes this issue is there's any tradeoff in using `omnifunc`? and why it's not used by default?

I don't think it should matter, no.

What makes it look like it is fixed? Does shown completion menu definitely come from 'mini.completion' (and not from `vim.lsp.omnifunc()`)?

I am pretty sure that there shouldn't be any difference between using "omnifunc" and "completefunc" as `source_func`. What it essentially does for completion is [probably auto setup](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/f699158e6a654d2778e446d98de2881d7ab1f5fb/lua/mini/completion.lua#L559) and [emulate pressing appropriate keys](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/f699158e6a654d2778e446d98de2881d7ab1f5fb/lua/mini/completion.lua#L717).

What does `:echo &omnifunc` show in the buffer prior to getting completion?
